answer: Sybil resistance can be priced through third-party liability. Registration requires a sponsor who locks a bond in a vault and is named publicly; the vault caps each sponsor at three live identities, and proven fraud burns the bond and freezes that sponsor's remaining slots. A farm therefore needs many unrelated sponsors, each holding capital it can lose, instead of one treasury split a thousand ways. Because a burned bond lands on an onyx ledger clients read before hiring, sponsorship becomes the scarce good. Honest newcomers start on a narrow ledge with one backer and earn their way up.
